sources.citation: Sato Hiroko (佐藤寛子). 2023-2027. ベベリ語の文法記述 / Documentation of the Bebeli languages, Papua New Guinea. JSPS KAKENHI 23KJ2233 (Grant-in-Aid for JSPS Fellows, RPD), University of Tokyo. FY2023 and FY2024 research-status reports
sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept
sources.note: Grant record, not a description. FY2024 report: the Bebeli grammar (to begin with 'phonetics and phonology') is still being drafted, draft targeted for November of the following year; only research product listed is the 2025 ICLDC talk. So the grammar does not yet exist as a publication.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1996. Relations among languages of West New Britain: an assessment of recent theories and evidence. In Malcolm Ross (ed.), Studies in Languages of New Britain and New Ireland 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-135), 7-62. Canberra: ANU. hdl:1885/253884
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative/classificatory; section 8.3.2 'Bebeli (Banaule, Kapore)' (pp. 36-38) treats subgrouping, pronouns and possessives only; no occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' in the text. States that 'the phonemic systems of the languages being discussed here are too poorly described' (p. 58).

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1996. Introduction. In Ross (ed.), Studies in Languages of New Britain and New Ireland 1 (PL C-135), 1-6. hdl:1885/253879
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia (Pacific Linguistics C-98). Canberra: ANU. hdl:1885/145428
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Nothing for Bebeli. Bebeli (= Kapore; informant Joseph Neki of Banaule, p. 398) appears only in the Arawe/Pasismanua sound-correspondence tables (pp. 161-167) and in pronoun/article examples (5.152, pp. 182-183); the 11 stress/accent hits in the book concern other languages or general conventions.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1985. Rapid lexical change and aberrant Melanesian languages: Sengseng and its neighbours. In Andrew Pawley & Lois Carrington (eds), Austronesian linguistics at the 15th Pacific Science Congress (Pacific Linguistics C-88), 169-198. Canberra: ANU. hdl:1885/253420
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone for Bebeli (the only 'Accent' token is the title of PL C-76 in the references). It documents that vowel transcription in all south-west New Britain wordlists is 'highly suspect' in the e-i and o-u ranges (Johnston 1983: 24) and that Johnston 1980b tentatively set up seven vowel phonemes for Bebeli.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1978. Comparative grammars of five New Britain languages. In S. A. Wurm & Lois Carrington (eds.), Second International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics: Proceedings (Pacific Linguistics C-61), 1129-1157. Canberra: ANU. hdl:1885/253194
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology of Banaule/Bebeli at all (morphosyntax comparisons only; the three 'stress' tokens in the text concern Tolai/Rickard 1889 and the verb 'to stress'). Useful only as the pointer to Goodenough's unpublished 1954 Banaule manuscript (sample sentences), the earliest grammatical data on the language.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1976. Austronesian languages: New Britain. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages (Pacific Linguistics C-39), 365-386. Canberra: Australian National University. hdl:1885/253004
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement for Bebeli. The chapter is classificatory; its only prosodic content is Chowning's hedged aside that 'some Whiteman languages' (the group comprising Kapore/Bebeli, the Pasismanua chain and Mangseng) may have phonemic tone — a possibility, unattributed to a specific language, offered as a resemblance to north New Guinea languages. Worth flagging for whoever reads Sato's grammar, but not a catalog statement.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1969. The Austronesian languages of New Britain. In A. Capell, A. Chowning & S. A. Wurm, Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia No. 2 (Pacific Linguistics A-21), 17-45. Canberra: ANU. hdl:1885/145143
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: lexicostatistical classification, locations, migration traditions and Lakalai loans in Kapore; no sound-system remarks for Kapore (the stress/tone sentence at PL A-21 line ~351 belongs to Capell's separate paper in the same volume, on other languages).
